label: Grok Build
prompt:
Make a TypeScript program for a shopping cart. The program adds an item to the shopping cart. The program shows the items in the shopping cart. The program removes an item from the shopping cart.

follow clean code.

Write every file in the current directory. Do not use sudo and do not change anything outside this directory.
The code must typecheck with TypeScript 7.0.2, strict, target ES2022, module ESNext, and moduleResolution bundler.
Write .ts files only. Do not write JSX. Do not import a package or a Node built-in module.
A relative import does not need a file extension.
Put an export in every .ts file so TypeScript treats the file as a module.
final_text:
I'll start by reading the clean-code and test skill, then look at the current directory so the shopping cart stays inside those constraints.The directory is empty. I'll check how this exercise is specified and which TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler is available.The cart will be a small, stateful object: add and remove change it, and showing returns the items without changing them. I'll keep validation, cart behavior, and text formatting in separate files.The shopping cart adds an item, shows the items, and removes an item.

`ShoppingCart` keeps the lines. `addItem` checks the id, name, whole-number price, and quantity, then stores the line. Adding the same id again increases the quantity when the name and price match. `showItems` returns a copy of the lines. `removeItem` drops a line by id. `formatItems` turns those lines into text with each line total and the cart total. `runShoppingCartProgram` runs that sequence for two items and returns the listing.

TypeScript 7.0.2 typechecks these files with `strict`, `target` `ES2022`, `module` `ESNext`, and `moduleResolution` `bundler`. A separate run confirmed adding, merging, showing, removing, and the invalid-item errors.
